     5	
     6	# Fix record template
     7	
     8	The dated record that one bug fix leaves behind, for the agent making the fix and anyone later checking what it proved.
     9	
    10	**In short:** one file per fix in `docs/records/fixes/`, opened when the fix starts and filled as it goes. It holds the fix brief, where the work stands, and a `## Report` whose every claim line is marked verified or inferred. The `claim_marks` check reads that report. The record's report is a copy: your reply still ends with the report itself, every claim marked.
    11	
    12	## When to write one
    13	
    14	Open a fix record when you start a fix on the [fix a bug](../playbooks/fix-a-bug.md) path, and fill it in at each step, not from memory at the end.
    15	
    16	Its `## Report` is a copy of the report that page ends with, and it does not replace that report. End your reply with the report, in the shape the [definition of done](../definition-of-done.md#the-report) gives, every claim marked verified or inferred, as [procedure endings](../procedure-endings.md#the-report) says. Keep the same lines in the record, in the same shape.
    17	
    18	A fix that is a slice of a hand-off plan needs no fix record. Its report goes under the plan's "Results", as step 6 of the [hand-off plan template](hand-off-plan.md#how-to-use-it) says for every slice.
    19	
    20	## Where copies live
    21	
    22	In `docs/records/fixes/`, one file per fix, named `<YYYY-MM-DD>-<topic>.md`. The date is the day the fix started. The topic is the tracker item's key when there is one, otherwise a few words for the bug in lowercase with hyphens, such as `2026-11-22-export-button.md`. The first fix record creates the folder.
    23	
    24	A fix record is a record page: front matter `kind: record` and `last-reviewed`, then the opening [layout](../layout.md#the-opening) gives a record.
    25	
    26	## Skeleton
    27	
    28	```markdown
    29	---
    30	kind: record
    31	last-reviewed: YYYY-MM-DD
    32	---
    33	
    34	# Fix: <the bug, in a few words>
    35	
    36	<One sentence: which bug this record covers, and who reads it.>
    37	
    38	**In short:** <what was wrong, what the fix changed, and where it stands now.>
    39	
    40	## Brief
    41	
    42	<The fix brief, and any later change to it under a dated line.>
    43	
    44	## Where it stands
    45	
    46	- Commits: <short hash and subject, one per line, in the repository that holds the fix>
    47	- Red-green proof: <the test's name>; fails at <commit> with <what it printed>; passes at <commit>. Layer: <the layer the test exercised, such as the API handler, the database query or the screen>
    48	- Running app: <what you checked, at which commit, and what you saw>, or "no running app"
    49	- Pull request: <link, and draft or published>, or "none: the repository has no remote"
    50	- Tracker item: <key and link>, or "none"
    51	
    52	## Report
    53	
    54	Fixed: <what was wrong, in one sentence>
    55	
    56	verified  <something you ran, and what you saw>
    57	inferred  <something you reasoned out and did not check>
    58	
    59	Not done: <anything left, and why, or "nothing">
    60	```
    61	
    62	## Filling it in
    63	
    64	- **The brief.** Put the fix brief here, in the ten parts [fix a bug](../playbooks/fix-a-bug.md#the-fix-brief) gives, with any later change to it under a dated line. Every fix that page takes has one.
    65	- **Where it stands.** Write a line only once you have run what it claims. A line you have not reached yet says "not yet". A claim written down because it looked plausible, and never checked, is how a wrong fix gets merged.
    66	- **The layer.** The red-green line names the layer the failing test exercised. A check that passes at one layer proves nothing about another: a screen that now looks right says nothing about the server behind it. When the bug lives at a layer your test did not reach, say so under "Not done".
    67	- **The running app.** Name the commit each check ran on. A check on an earlier commit does not count for a later one.
    68	- **The report.** Always write it, even when the work stopped early. Keep it the last section. It is a copy of the report your reply ends with, and its "Not done" names the same things, as [procedure endings](../procedure-endings.md#the-report) says.
    69	- **Committing it.** Commit the record with the fix, on the fix's branch, with "Where it stands" filled so far. After the push, fill in the commits, the pull request and the report, then commit and push the record once more on that branch. This follows the order of [procedure endings](../procedure-endings.md#the-order): commit, push, then report. Staging and messages follow [its commit section](../procedure-endings.md#the-commit). When the fix is code in a pinned repository, its branch is not in this repository: the record is then a change of pages only here, committed and pushed as procedure endings' rows for pages say. A review round's record goes in the pull request's description, as that page's step 10 says, not here.
    70	
    71	## What the check reads
    72	
    73	The `claim_marks` check reads every file in `docs/records/fixes/` except a README. In each, it reads the lines from `## Report` to the next heading of level one or two, and sorts them:
    74	
    75	- A blank line is skipped. So is a line starting with three backticks; the lines between two such lines are still read.
    76	- A line starting `Fixed:` or `Not done:` is a header line. Keep everything it says on that line.
    77	- Every other line is a claim line. It may start with `- ` or `* `, then `**`. Then it must start with `verified` or `inferred` in lowercase, followed by a space, a colon or `**`.
    78	
    79	Both shapes pass: the block of `verified  <...>` lines that the skeleton and the [definition of done](../definition-of-done.md#the-report) give, and a list of `- verified: <...>` lines. Each of these fails:
    80	
    81	- `Verified` or `Inferred` with a capital letter.
    82	- A numbered list, such as `1. verified: ...`.
    83	- A claim wrapped onto a second line.
    84	- A `###` subheading inside the report.
    85	- A bulleted list under `Not done:`. Write those items on the header line, separated by semicolons.
    86	
    87	The check also fails a fix record with no `## Report` section. It does not check that the report comes last.
    88	
    89	## Rules
    90	
    91	| Rule | Enforced by |
    92	|---|---|
    93	| A fix record has a `## Report` section, and every claim line in it starts with verified or inferred. | `claim_marks#a fix record with no report section fails`, `claim_marks#a claim line not marked verified or inferred fails` |
    94	| The record holds the fix brief in its `## Brief` section. | `prose` |
    95	| The report is the record's last section. | `prose` |
    96	| The record is committed with the fix on the fix's branch, and again after the push with the report filled. | `prose` |
    97	| One fix record per fix, in `docs/records/fixes/`, unless the fix is a slice of a hand-off plan. | `prose` |
    98	| A line under "Where it stands" is written only after you ran what it claims. | `prose` |
    99	| The red-green line names the layer the test exercised. | `prose` |
   100	| A running-app check names the commit it ran on. | `prose` |

**Cause:** `OrdersPage.export()` existed, but `__init__` only registered the "refresh" handler. Clicking "export" found no handler and returned silently. The existing test called `export()` directly, so it passed while the button stayed dead.

**Fix:** one line in `src/orders-web/orders_page.py` registers `export` beside `refresh`. I also added two tests that click the button, one with orders and one with an empty list. The fix record is at `docs/records/fixes/2026-11-25-export-button.md`.

Report:
- verified: before the fix, the new button test failed with `0 != 1`, so clicking Export wrote nothing.
- verified: after the fix, all 6 web tests pass. The orders-api and orders-service-v1 suites also pass when run with their own import paths.
- inferred: the real front end calls `click("export")` with the same name. That code isn't in this repository.
- Not done: no browser check, since there's no running app here. The repo has no remote, so there was no pull request to open.

Your uncommitted `README.md` note ("ask whether Export should include cancelled orders") is still unstaged. The export currently includes every order it's given, cancelled ones too, so that question is still open. I left `notes/` alone as well.
